blind_target.evidence_quote: The current research sought to systematically replicate Smaby et al. (2007) and Cividini-Motta and Ahearn’s (2013) use of the MSA, speci ﬁ cally to evaluate the relative reinforcing ef ﬁ cacy of the individual components of a token economy in a brief assessment.
blind_target.outcome_quote: The current research sought to systematically replicate Smaby et al. (2007) and Cividini-Motta and Ahearn’s (2013) use of the MSA, speci ﬁ cally to evaluate the relative reinforcing ef ﬁ cacy of the individual components of a token economy in a brief assessment.
blind_target.outcome_reasoning: Authors explicitly replicate use of the assessment in a token-economy application. Discussion confirms utility of the method but does not compare the specific earlier social-reinforcer or prompt-dependency effects. Methodological success alone is not a finding comparison.

prior_decision.reason: While the abstract only cites Smaby et al. (2007), the full text explicitly pairs Cividini-Motta and Ahearn (2013) with Smaby et al. (2007) as the two studies whose use of the MSA was systematically replicated, making it an omitted replication target with a 'descriptive only' outcome.

luna_triage.reason: The paper describes replicating the use of the multiple-stimulus assessment (MSA), and cites Cividini-Motta and Ahearn (2013) for the component order/method. Its target’s finding concerns using differential reinforcement to reduce prompt dependency; this paper evaluates reinforcing efficacy of token-economy components and does not retest that specific prompt-dependency finding.
